# Publish partial work as a draft PR, and refuse workflow-file changes

One part of the GitHub Actions workflow work. **Treat this request as self-contained**: everything needed is below. Don't assume access to any other issue or to `docs/specs/github-actions-workflow.md`.

**Order:** builds on `jig github implement`, which already opens a ready PR for a completed run and comments when nothing changed.

## What

When a run started from an issue cannot finish but did produce changes, jig opens a **draft** PR. One PR comment lists what is still open: the reviewer's unresolved findings, final-check gaps and verification failures. If the run's changes touch anything under `.github/workflows/`, jig publishes nothing and explains on the issue that this automation cannot change workflows.

## Why

Attempts cost time and money. A run that ran out of attempts often leaves useful work and the exact list of what is wrong; throwing both away means a person starts from zero. Workflow files decide what runs with the repository's credentials, so the automation must never ship changes to them.

## Context

jig is a Node CLI (TypeScript, Vitest) that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has one agent implement and another review each slice inside a Docker sandbox, and lands them on one run branch, `jig/run/<id>`. Before editing, read `README.md`, `docs/architecture.html`, `CLAUDE.md`, and every `.claude/rules/` file that covers a file you will change, specs included.

The layering is domain rules (`src/domain/`) → flows and steps (`src/flow/`, `src/steps/`) → ports (`src/ports/`) → adapters (`src/adapters/`). Composition lives in `src/app/` and commands in `src/cli/`. Specs sit beside the code as `*.spec.ts` and pass fakes for ports, never module mocks. Anything that touches git is tested against a real temporary repository (`tests/support/temp-repo.ts`).

This issue is one part of the GitHub Actions workflow. In that workflow an operator marks GitHub issues ready, and jig, running in GitHub Actions under a GitHub App identity, implements them, opens PRs and works on review feedback. The jig core, called the *execution engine* (plan, implement, verify, review), stays independent of GitHub. The GitHub code is an *integration*: optional, jig-owned code in its own directory (`src/integrations/github/` unless one already exists). It depends on core contracts, and the core never imports it. jig must start without the integration or its credentials.

- `jig github implement --issue <n>` exists, with its GitHub port, orchestration state ref and publication receipts.
- Run state records why a run stopped: which cap was hit, on which slice, after how many attempts (`src/domain/run-state.ts`, `result.json`).
- Review feedback is free text today (`src/steps/slice.ts`); final-check results live in `src/domain/final-check.ts`.

## Target

- An outcome of `stuck` with commits on the run branch beyond the starting commit opens a draft PR (same head, base and body rules as a ready PR) plus one PR-level comment with the remaining findings, final-check gaps and the last verification failure.
- Findings are published **at PR level only**. Keep any file and line a finding mentions as text, and never invent an inline anchor. Inline placement is a later issue.
- Before any publication, check the change set (default branch fork point to run head). Any added, modified or deleted path under `.github/workflows/` means: publish nothing, comment on the issue naming the files, and record the refusal in orchestration state.
- The comment is repeatable without duplicates, through a receipt in orchestration state.

## Don't undo these

- **Agents and project commands run only inside the sandbox.** Never on the runner host, not even "for CI".
- **Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line, the image, or the sandbox.** The App key and the publishing token stay in the host process.
- **The core never imports the GitHub integration.** Dependencies point from the integration toward core contracts.
- **The host publishes, not the sandbox.** Pushes, PRs and comments are made by the GitHub integration in the host process.
- **No automatic merge.** A person merges every PR. `mergeMode` does not apply to runs this automation starts.

## Done when

- [ ] A stuck run with commits opens one draft PR and one findings comment; a rerun adds neither again
- [ ] A stuck run with no commits opens no PR and comments on the issue
- [ ] A run that changes `.github/workflows/ci.yml` publishes nothing and the issue comment names the file
- [ ] `npm run validate` passes from the repository root


Source: https://github.com/ygrishajev/jig/issues/14

docs.design:
# Design

## Goal

Publish useful partial work from issue runs as a draft PR with one repeatable PR-level findings comment. Refuse publication whenever the run’s change set contains a path under `.github/workflows/`, explain the refusal on the issue, and persist that decision.

## Context

The GitHub integration already owns issue snapshots, publication rules and orchestration receipts. `implementIssue` invokes `runJig` with `merge:false` and required remote persistence. Completed runs with net changes receive ready PRs; other outcomes receive issue comments. `GithubPort` already supports draft PRs and issue-style comments, which also work at PR level.

Two existing behaviors need particular care. First, `hasChangesAgainst` measures a net diff, whereas partial-work eligibility requires commits beyond the starting revision. Second, `GitRemoteRunStore.save` pushes the run branch during execution, before the integration decides whether publication is permitted. A guard only around PR creation would therefore be insufficient.

Review and verification feedback currently share slice feedback fields. Final-check state retains gaps and verification status but drops verification output. Historical feedback cannot safely be treated as unresolved findings.

## Chosen approach

### Separate checkpoint persistence from code publication

Introduce a generic deferred branch-publication policy for integration-started runs. Wire it through the application and built-in remote store without importing GitHub integration code into core. Persist the policy with the run so retries through another entry point cannot accidentally restore automatic branch pushes. Normal CLI runs retain their current persistence behavior.

Deferred saves push only state metadata, using existing leased updates. They must not push run commits through another branch, hidden ref, checkpoint parent or bundle. Record the exact local run head associated with each checkpoint separately from the numeric state revision. Persist an immutable starting commit before implementation begins.

Remote metadata alone cannot recover unpublished code on a fresh runner. Loading a deferred checkpoint must verify that its required code revision exists locally or is already available on the published run branch. If unavailable, return an actionable Result error rather than resuming state against the default branch or silently restarting. Local retries retain their unpublished work; fresh-runner recovery before publication requires preserving that local repository. This limitation is explicit rather than disguising code publication as checkpoint storage.

### Inspect and publish one exact revision

The host integration obtains a publication snapshot containing the immutable run head, starting commit, default-branch revision and merge base. Partial-work eligibility checks that the head contains commits beyond the starting commit; it does not substitute a net-diff check. Completed-run eligibility retains its existing net-change behavior.

Use a NUL-delimited git path diff from the default-branch merge base to the exact run head. Disable rename detection so moves become deletion/addition pairs and both paths are inspected. Include every changed path, including type changes, and refuse any path with the exact `.github/workflows/` prefix. Git failures, missing required revisions and invalid ancestry fail closed.

The integration owns the workflow restriction; the git adapter owns revision and path inspection. A host publication operation owns the inspection-before-push ordering and pushes the inspected object ID, with a lease, rather than resolving a mutable branch name again. Apply the guard to ready and draft publication and before reusing publication receipts. No rejected revision is pushed, and no PR or findings comment is created for it.

On refusal, persist a record keyed by run and head containing the offending paths and inspected base information. Then post a receipt-protected issue comment naming those paths and explaining that this automation cannot change workflows. A recorded refusal without a comment receipt retries the comment. It does not imply the comment succeeded.

### Publish stuck runs and diagnostics

Extend the existing publication decision: `stuck` plus commits beyond the starting revision creates a draft PR using the existing head, base, title and body rules. A stuck run without commits retains the issue-comment path. Other incomplete outcomes keep their existing behavior.

After ensuring the PR exists, ensure its findings comment exists independently. A saved PR receipt must never bypass that second operation. Use the PR number with the issue-style comment API; do not introduce review comments or inline anchors.

Expose a core-owned diagnostic projection that provides the stop reason, unresolved reviewer feedback, outstanding final-check gaps and the last verification failure. Retain reviewer feedback separately from generic last feedback so a subsequent implementation or verification failure does not erase an unresolved review. Clear unresolved review data on approval. Persist verification command, bounded output and ordering information at the point of failure; retain enough information to distinguish a final-check failure from a later repair-slice failure. Preserve existing observation metadata. Identify a historical last failure as such if a later verification passed.

Add optional fields with backward-compatible schema defaults. Legacy records report available diagnostics and explicitly identify missing output; do not infer unresolved findings by replaying free-text feedback history. Keep file and line references as plain text in a single PR-level comment. Render free text safely, bound diagnostic output, and avoid duplicating the same verification failure across sections.

### Make publication retryable

Extend orchestration state with separate findings-comment receipts and workflow-refusal records. Comment identity includes its purpose and target as well as run, outcome and exact code revision, preventing collisions with existing status comments. Keep existing PR receipts compatible.

Receipts prevent ordinary rerun duplicates. To recover a comment posted before its receipt was saved, give integration comments a deterministic marker and add a narrow GitHub lookup capability for that marker. Reconcile before creating a comment, then save its receipt. Serialize publication for the same accepted request using orchestration ownership backed by leased updates so concurrent invocations cannot both pass the lookup and post. PR recovery continues to use head lookup. Failed API or receipt writes return Result errors and leave independently completed work reusable.

## Alternatives considered

1. **Add draft support and check workflow paths immediately before opening a PR.** Rejected because checkpoint persistence has already pushed the code, violating the refusal boundary. It also leaves PR receipts able to suppress retries of missing findings comments.
2. **Persist unpublished code on a hidden remote ref or inside checkpoint artifacts.** Rejected because hidden refs and bundles still transmit the forbidden changes. They would preserve fresh-runner recovery by weakening the publication prohibition.
3. **Disable remote persistence entirely for issue runs.** Rejected because the integration requires durable remote state and orchestration receipts. Metadata-only checkpoints preserve that requirement while explicitly detecting unavailable code during recovery.

## Assumptions

- The prohibition permits orchestration metadata, diagnostic state and the required refusal comment, but prohibits transmitting unapproved repository code. State commits must remain independent of run-code ancestry.
- A change set means the net merge-base-to-head diff specified by the request. A workflow edit fully reverted before the inspected head is outside that change set.
- A run with commits but no net diff remains eligible under the requested stuck-run rule. If GitHub refuses that PR, surface the API failure without claiming publication succeeded or changing eligibility silently.
- Existing state remains readable. If a legacy run lacks a trustworthy starting commit or required unpublished revision, fail explicitly rather than inventing one from the current default branch.
- Existing remote publication cannot be undone by this change; legacy runs are checked before any further publication.

## Non-goals

- Inline review placement, inferred file anchors or structured parsing of reviewer prose.
- Automatic merging, draft promotion, review-feedback implementation or new workflow automation.
- Fresh-runner recovery of code that has deliberately never been transmitted.
- Rewriting, deleting or reverting previously published branches and PRs.
- Moving agents or project commands onto the host, or exposing GitHub publishing credentials to the sandbox.

## Affected areas

- `src/integrations/github/`: publication orchestration, workflow policy, comment rendering, orchestration schemas and receipts, GitHub comment reconciliation, and adjacent specs.
- `src/app/run-jig.ts`, `src/app/run-stores.ts`, and relevant composition: deferred persistence wiring and safe resume behavior.
- `src/adapters/run-store/git-remote-run-store.ts`, composite/local store behavior where necessary, and adjacent specs: metadata-only checkpoints and code-revision validation.
- `src/adapters/git/`: immutable publication snapshots, changed-path inspection and leased exact-revision pushes, tested against real repositories.
- `src/domain/run-state.ts`, `src/domain/slice.ts`, `src/domain/final-check.ts`, relevant outcomes, reducers and steps: starting revision and durable diagnostics with backward-compatible parsing.
- Existing fakes and shared builders, `README.md`, `docs/commands.md`, and persistence documentation affected by deferred recovery semantics.

# Plan

## Step 1 — Separate remote checkpoints from branch publication

Introduce and wire a generic deferred publication policy for GitHub-started runs while retaining `merge:false` and required remote state persistence. Persist the policy, immutable starting commit and checkpoint code revision. Make deferred saves push metadata only, without linking state commits to unpublished code. Keep ordinary CLI persistence unchanged.

Implement load-time validation across composite-store selection so no state can resume against missing or mismatched code. Allow local retries with retained objects and recovery from an already published revision; return a typed, actionable error when a fresh runner lacks unpublished code. Define conservative legacy handling without guessing a starting revision.

Test save, load, interruption and resume using real temporary repositories and a bare remote. Verify that deferred saves do not create or advance the run branch or make its code reachable through state refs; verify normal persistence remains unchanged and missing-code recovery fails explicitly.

## Step 2 — Guard exact-revision publication and record workflow refusals

Add git adapter operations that resolve the run head, validate commits beyond its starting point, resolve the default-branch merge base and return NUL-delimited changed paths with rename detection disabled. Keep completed-run net-change eligibility separate from stuck-run commit eligibility.

Implement a host integration publication operation that owns inspection and leased publication of the exact inspected object ID. Route all issue-run branch publication through it. Fail closed on inspection errors and inspect before receipt reuse.

Extend orchestration state with backward-compatible refusal records and independent refusal-comment receipts. Persist a refusal before attempting its issue comment; name all offending paths and retry a missing comment without publishing code.

Test additions, modifications, deletions, type changes, renames into and out of the workflow directory, unusual filenames, similarly named allowed paths, divergent default-branch history, git failures and branch movement after inspection. Assert refused code never reaches the remote run branch and no PR or findings comment is created.

## Step 3 — Preserve and expose remaining diagnostics

Add core-owned persisted fields and a diagnostic projection for unresolved reviewer feedback, outstanding final-check gaps and the last verification failure. Capture bounded verification output in slice and final-check transitions, preserve existing observations, and record enough ordering information to identify the latest failure during repair work.

Keep unresolved reviewer feedback through subsequent implementation and verification attempts, clear it on approval, and exclude resolved feedback history. Distinguish historical verification failures from current gaps. Preserve free-text file and line references and report unavailable legacy output honestly.

Test review rejection followed by other failures, later approval, final-check repair failures, successful later checks, serialization and legacy schema loading. Exercise the transitions through existing fake ports rather than module mocks.

## Step 4 — Publish draft PRs and independently reconcile findings comments

Extend `publicationFor` and its orchestration so stuck runs with commits open draft PRs using existing head, base, title and body rules. Keep stuck runs without commits on the issue-comment path and preserve completed and other outcome behavior.

Add separate findings-comment receipts keyed to purpose, PR target, run, outcome and exact revision. After creating or reusing a PR, always process a missing findings receipt. Render one PR-level comment from the diagnostic projection, including the stop reason and preserving references as text.

Add deterministic comment markers and a narrow lookup method to the GitHub port, adapter and fake. Reconcile comments after uncertain API or receipt outcomes. Use leased orchestration ownership to serialize publication for an accepted request and release ownership through one lifecycle wrapper.

Test one draft and one comment across reruns, PR success followed by comment failure, comment success followed by receipt failure, concurrent publication attempts, refusal-comment recovery, and legacy receipts. Verify no inline-comment APIs are used and that GitHub refusal of a commit-bearing zero-diff PR is surfaced accurately.

## Step 5 — Verify integrated behavior and document recovery limits

Extend the existing `implement-issue.spec.ts` scenarios through the real execution flow with `FakeGithub`, `FakeAgentSession` and temporary repositories. Cover stuck runs with and without commits, ready-PR regression behavior, persisted diagnostic output, repeated workflow refusals, retry after approved branch publication and fresh-runner failure before publication when code is unavailable.

Retain assertions for sandbox-only agents and project commands, host-only publishing credentials, integration-to-core dependency direction, required state storage and disabled automatic merging. Follow setup-based testing conventions and use shared generated builders.

Update command and persistence documentation to describe draft eligibility, PR-level findings, workflow refusal, independent retry receipts and the deferred-code recovery limitation. Ensure the README’s draft claim matches implemented behavior.

Run focused specs during implementation, then run `npm run validate` from the repository root. Resolve failures in build, typecheck, lint, duplication, formatting, coverage and secretlint before completion.

feedbackHistory:
1. src/integrations/github/octokit-github.ts:111 — commentOnIssue uses the generic retrying call, so a POST that succeeds remotely but returns an unavailable response is posted again before commentOnce can reconcile its marker. Make comment creation single-attempt or reconcile the marker before each retry. Add an adapter-level lost-response test; FakeGithub currently bypasses this retry behavior.
2. src/adapters/run-store/composite-run-store.ts:53 — Checkpoint consistency validation returns early when the selected copy lacks codeRevision or deferred policy. Equal-revision copies therefore produce different results depending on store order, potentially accepting state without validating its code. Validate tied copies before these guards, including checkpoint presence and publication policy, and apply consistency validation to peek selection too. Add tests with reversed store ordering and missing checkpoints.
3. src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:52 — Publication ownership expires after 15 minutes without renewal or subsequent ownership checks. A slow publisher can continue after another job acquires the expired lease, allowing concurrent comments or PR creation. Maintain ownership throughout publication and stop publication after ownership is lost. Add a deterministic test where the first publisher remains active across expiry while a second attempts publication.
4. src/integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts:63 — A panic or rejected callback skips ownership release, contradicting the required lifecycle wrapper and its documented guarantee. Release ownership in finally while preserving the original panic and the existing Result cleanup precedence. Add a test proving another publisher can acquire ownership immediately after callback failure.

The protected-file changes are required by the slice and do not independently weaken existing checks; removed repository-helper coverage is replaced by history/publication coverage. The recorded validation result was considered; no verification command or broader suite was rerun.

1. src/adapters/git/run-code.ts:68 — Restore checked-out run branches through their worktree rather than updating the ref alone. A focused real-repository check showed restore returning success while leaving the worktree with staged reverse changes because its index and files still represented the old commit. Preserve dirty work and add coverage for restoring a checkpoint with an existing worktree.
2. src/adapters/git/repository.spec.ts:95 (deleted test) — Preserve the removed empty-commit regression check in the replacement publication specs. The new unchanged-publication test uses the starting commit itself, so it no longer establishes that commits with unchanged trees are ineligible for completed-run publication. Add a real-repository test showing an empty commit yields unchanged publication while counting as work beyond the starting commit.
3. src/adapters/git/run-code.ts:23,27,44,67 and src/ports/run-code.ts:9,14 — Narrow the error types instead of reusing RunStoreFailure, as required by errors-as-values.md. checkpoint and moveBranch only return GitCommandFailed; restore and ensureAvailable should declare their actual error unions, excluding unrelated configuration and local-state write errors.
4. src/integrations/github/implement-issue.ts:175 — Narrow codeRevisionOf's error type to RunStoreFailure. Its body cannot return the many agent, sandbox and merge errors included in JigError; errors-as-values.md requires the union of errors the body can actually return.

feedbackHistory: 1. src/domain/final-check.ts:136–137: Preserve legacy final-check verification failures when a later check passes. Add a regression test covering legacy loading, successful repair verification, serialization/reload, and the historical diagnostic projection.
